youtube_title: Swept Away by a River Current: Swim Against It or Float? Brave vs Normal #11 #Shorts
youtube_description:
BRAVE vs NORMAL - WHO'S RIGHT? #11. On a trek you slip while crossing a river and the current sweeps you away. Brave swims hard against the current. Normal floats on his back, feet first. Who's right?
Answer: Normal. River safety advice (Water Safety NZ, US National Park Service): don't fight the current - you tire fast. Float on your back with your feet pointing downstream to push off rocks, keep your head up, never try to stand up in fast water (a foot can get trapped under rocks), and work your way slowly towards the bank.
Source: Water Safety NZ survival swimming; US NPS river safety tips.
